cluster_summary: Judged from code, the real open ground in this cluster is narrow. It is gazette-translated-indexed's test-backed amend/supersede citation graph across ~53 ministries, which no official tool (eGazette, India Code, Indian Kanoon) provides, and CBSE_paper_patterns' year-deduplicated, marks-weighted recurrence index over a 30.7k-question corpus. lok-rajya-sabha-qa adds a real 18th-LS + Rajya Sabha extension of TCPD-IPD and a novel PQ-vs-PIB scrutiny join, but its methods are simple: lift ratios, Louvain and unigram counts. The biggest README-vs-code gaps are these. kalki_flooding's IUDX archive holds no observations (access pending), and its real analysis is an undocumented IMD-rainfall study. The two mospi repos contain no code (their outputs came from an MCP session), and the private one is a 97% blob-identical duplicate of -public. india-govt-yellow-pages' 'DDD/Graphify' layer is a stub over CSVs. jai_kisan_jai_javan's README advertises ~30 files that don't exist, and jal_jeevan_lottery's JJM and lottery-market baselines are off ~3x and more than 10x against official figures. Neither docs-only repo engages the binding constraints (Lotteries Act 1998 state-only rule; FCI is not a meal processor and DFRL owns ration technology). Two risk flags: india-govt-yellow-pages publicly republishes de-obfuscated contact details of named officials (privacy/DPDP), and CBSE_paper_patterns redistributes the full CBSE/NCERT text despite its description saying papers are not redistributed. india-election-analysis cites a 'Mitra 2026 PLOS ONE' model that could not be verified, and its implementation is a simplified bloc-mean.

repos.does: Builds a SQLite citation graph of Government of India gazette notifications (what each notification amends, supersedes, corrects) across ~53 ministries: fetches official PDFs from egazette.gov.in by gazette ID, extracts text, runs regex/anchor 'drafting template' matchers (5 shared templates + ~40 per-ministry modules) to propose cross-reference candidates, stores hand-verified rows in per-ministry SQL seed files, and renders HTML pages, an LLM-ready JSONL export and Gemini/LibreTranslate translations of the project's own metadata.

snippets.code:
lift_rows = []
    for party, counter in party_ministry.items():
        party_share = party_question_count[party] / total_questions
        for ministry, cnt in counter.items():
            expected = ministry_total[ministry] * party_share
            lift = cnt / expected if expected > 0 else 0
            lift_rows.append(
                {
                    "party": party,
                    "ministry": ministry,
                    "questions": cnt,
                    "ministry_total": ministry_total[ministry],
                    "party_total": party_question_count[party],
                    "lift": round(lift, 3),
                }
            )
    lift_rows.sort(key=lambda r: (-r["lift"], -r["questions"]))
snippets.why: 'Signature ministry' = observed party×ministry questions over the count expected from the party's overall share (a lift/observed-over-expected ratio). This is the repo's core metric, a simple cross-tab statistic rather than anything TCPD-IPD or PRS publish.
Party communities come from cosine similarity of lift vectors (edge if >0.15) followed by Louvain (Blondel et al. 2008), so clustering runs on relative emphasis rather than raw volume.

snippets.code:
def backfill_days(con, resource_id, now):
    """Dynamic first-grant backfill depth: cover the whole approval wait.

    Anchored to the sensor's earliest access_log entry (the first time this
    collector ever tried it), clamped to [MIN_BACKFILL_DAYS, MAX_BACKFILL_DAYS].
    """
    first_try = con.execute(
        "SELECT min(run_ts) FROM access_log WHERE resource_id=?", [resource_id]
    ).fetchone()[0]
    if first_try is None:
        return MIN_BACKFILL_DAYS
    if first_try.tzinfo is None:
        # duckdb stores our aware-UTC inserts as LOCAL-naive (verified: the
        # 03:21 UTC run reads back as 08:51 IST) — reattach the local zone,
        # not UTC, or every wait is undercounted by the UTC offset
        first_try = first_try.replace(tzinfo=datetime.now().astimezone().tzinfo)
    waited = math.ceil((now - first_try).total_seconds() / 86400)
    return max(MIN_BACKFILL_DAYS, min(waited, MAX_BACKFILL_DAYS))
snippets.why: The collector's distinctive logic: a backfill window sized to how long the provider took to approve access, clamped 7-30 days. This archiving of live-only IUDX snapshots is the novel part.

repos.does: Parses ~2k CBSE Class-XII board papers (pdftotext with page-level reprint dedupe, macOS Vision OCR for scans) into a 30.7k-question table with regex-parsed marks. Questions are classified by: (1) mining 2-4-word n-grams in ≥4-mark questions that recur across ≥3 distinct exam years, split into content topics vs generic stem formulas, giving a marks-weighted 'repetition index'; (2) Bloom level via command-verb regex lexicons with highest-level-wins, compared to CBSE's declared typology %; (3) TF-IDF cosine ≥0.80 near-duplicate detection across years; (4) all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding assignment of questions to syllabus units (cosine floor 0.28), validated against keyword gold sets (54-78% accurate, reported honestly).

repos.does: Python scripts that build Excel workbooks. The election-data analysis computes electors per constituency and a population-per-seat index. The coalition game theory computes exact Banzhaf indices, minimal winning coalitions and a 20k-draw Monte Carlo of seat permutations, with a seat-total sweep (534-1000) of Gallagher disproportionality. Vote-share modelling on TCPD Lok Dhaba covers a win/lose classifier, a PyMC hierarchical model with state partial pooling, and a 'Dirichlet Swing Matrix' model, all evaluated chronologically against a no-change baseline. There is also a women's-reservation seat-placement optimiser.

snippets.code:
def predict_with_swing_matrix(prior_df, transition_matrix_alpha, blocs=BLOCS):
    prior_shares = prior_df[blocs].values
    origin_idx = np.argmax(prior_shares, axis=1)
    preds = np.zeros_like(prior_shares)
    for k in range(len(blocs)):
        alpha_k = transition_matrix_alpha[k]
        dirichlet_mean = alpha_k / alpha_k.sum()
        mask = origin_idx == k
        preds[mask] = dirichlet_mean
    return preds
snippets.why: The 'swing matrix' prediction step. Each constituency gets its origin bloc's Dirichlet mean regardless of its own prior shares. That shows the model is a bloc-level average rather than a transition matrix applied to prior vote shares, which explains why it can't beat the no-change baseline.
